runs.market_commentary:
Asian markets staged a broad and deep risk-off session overnight, led by a Nikkei 225 collapse of 4.77% to 56,606 — its worst single-day percentage decline since mid-2025. The selloff was concentrated in semiconductors and AI hardware names after Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing slid 4.2% in Taipei, dragging the entire chip ecosystem lower and amplifying fears that AI-related capex spending is peaking. South Korea's KOSPI fell approximately 5.0%, reflecting the region's heavy semiconductor export exposure. The sharp moves came just one day after Anthropic (ANT) debuted on the Nasdaq at $111.50 — far above its $83 IPO price — only to close at $97 and slide another 6%+ in pre-market Friday trading, cooling the AI euphoria that had gripped markets for most of Q3.

European markets opened weaker across the board in sympathy, with the DAX shedding 1.56% to 25,101 and the FTSE 100 declining 0.39% to 10,411. The more modest European moves reflect the region's lower direct AI and semiconductor exposure, though financials and industrials were dragged by a stronger US dollar (DXY 103.93, a fresh 2026 high) and rising Treasury yields. The 10-year US Treasury yield stands at 5.05% as markets now price approximately 96% odds of a December Fed rate hike, following Thursday's FOMC minutes revealing two voting members already pushed for an immediate increase. The Philadelphia Fed manufacturing index shattered expectations, printing 6.3 against a prior reading of 20.9 — a dramatic signal of industrial slowdown that paradoxically added to stagflation fears.

US pre-market action is decisively bearish heading into Friday's open: Nasdaq 100 futures are down 1.49%, S&P 500 futures are off 0.65%, while Dow futures are marginally negative at -0.14%, holding around the 49,250 area. The Dow's breach below 50,000 on Thursday — for the first time since June — is raising technical alarm bells, with futures now targeting 48,500 support. AMD is leading the chip wreckage with another 7% decline pre-market. Meanwhile, earnings reporters offered some relief: Ross Stores beat Q3 estimates with comparable-store sales surging 8%, and Gap delivered a narrow beat. Intuit was the standout negative, guiding Q2 EPS far below consensus ($3.17-$3.22 vs. $3.98 estimated) and sliding over 10% pre-market. Gold slid to a 14-month low of $3,657 as the stronger dollar and rate hike expectations pressured the metal.

ideas.catalyst: Intuit Q1 beat was overshadowed by catastrophic Q2 EPS guidance of $3.17-$3.22 vs. the $3.98 consensus estimate, sending shares down 10%+ pre-market.
ideas.thesis: A guidance miss of this magnitude — $0.76/share below the Street's Q2 estimate — is not a minor revision; it signals underlying demand deterioration in Intuit's small-business and consumer segments that likely persists into the back half of fiscal 2027. At elevated software multiples, any forward estimate reset creates a double compression of earnings AND multiple, historically producing outsized downside moves over a 2-4 week horizon.
ideas.key_risk: Any Fed pivot signal or upside Q2 actual print could trigger a violent short squeeze in a heavily-shorted name.

ideas.theme: Asia Chip Selloff / AI Capex Rationalization
ideas.catalyst: AMD is down another 7% pre-market Friday, extending Thursday's losses as Taiwan Semiconductor slides 4.2% and the broader Asia semiconductor index collapses following Anthropic's IPO-day disappointment.
ideas.thesis: AMD's AI GPU business remains secondary to Nvidia's ecosystem lock-in, making it more vulnerable to any AI spending slowdown than its share price implies. With Anthropic's debut cooling AI sentiment and the Nasdaq 100 at risk of breaking 25,000, AMD's elevated forward P/E (~35x) leaves significant downside room before value buyers step in; the chart shows no technical support until the $140 area.
ideas.key_risk: Nvidia upgrade cycle benefiting AMD in server co-deployments could provide a floor; a surprise AI spending reaffirmation from a major hyperscaler would squeeze shorts hard.

ideas.theme: AI Infrastructure / Analyst Upgrade on Dip
ideas.catalyst: Seeking Alpha reports Nvidia and Nebius Group both received analyst upgrades Friday morning as analysts cite compelling value following the sharp AI-driven selloff, with the broader Nasdaq 100 down 1.49% pre-market providing a potential flush-and-recover entry.
ideas.thesis: Unlike AMD, Nvidia's moat in AI training (H200/B200 dominance) and software ecosystem (CUDA) means any AI capex cycle continuation directly flows to its top line; Anthropic's IPO uncertainty clouds AI sentiment short-term but does not alter the multi-year hyperscaler infrastructure buildout thesis. A flush to the $120-$125 zone — where multiple analysts have price targets — sets up a 15-20% recovery once the broader market stabilizes around the December Fed meeting.
ideas.key_risk: If the December Fed hike tips the economy into a sharper slowdown, hyperscaler capex guidance gets cut in Q1 earnings season, compressing Nvidia's forward multiple significantly.

sources.label: SA Analyst Upgrades — NVDA, NBIS, SHOP, GM

ideas.catalyst: Anthropic (ANT) opened at $111.50 on its IPO debut Thursday, closed at $97 — well below the intraday high — and is now down another 6% pre-market Friday, suggesting the $1.8 trillion valuation is facing sustained selling pressure from early flippers.
ideas.thesis: With a $1.8 trillion fully-diluted valuation on a company with limited disclosed revenue, ANT trades at a multiple that makes even Nvidia look cheap; institutional IPO allocations that received shares at $83 are sitting on paper gains and represent a natural, persistent supply overhang for weeks post-debut. The broader market environment — rising rates, tech selloff, cooling AI sentiment — creates a doubly adverse backdrop for what is essentially a speculative AI infrastructure bet.
ideas.key_risk: William Blair's Outperform initiation and any large-scale enterprise contract announcements could anchor the stock and trigger a short squeeze given limited borrow availability in a new IPO.

ideas.catalyst: Ross Stores reported Q3 EPS of $1.91 vs. $1.88 estimate on comparable-store sales growth of 8%, demonstrating that value-oriented consumers continue to trade down aggressively in the face of elevated prices and rising interest rates.
ideas.thesis: In a 5.05% 10-year yield environment heading into a probable December Fed hike, consumers are under meaningful real wage pressure, and discount retailers like Ross structurally benefit from the trade-down effect; the 8% comps growth is particularly impressive given the volatile macro backdrop, and suggests category-wide share gains from full-price competitors. Q4 guidance slightly below consensus is a typical conservative kitchen-sink approach heading into holiday, and the stock likely opens at a reasonable entry point post-earnings.
ideas.key_risk: If the Fed achieves a soft landing faster than expected, consumers could quickly re-trade up and compress Ross's outsized comps growth; weather disruption during peak holiday inventory clearance also poses seasonal risk.

ideas.catalyst: Palo Alto Networks was the top gainer in the S&P 500 on Thursday at approximately +6.4%, breaking from the broader tech selloff as cybersecurity spending proves sticky regardless of the AI valuation reset.
ideas.thesis: Enterprise cybersecurity budgets are increasingly non-discretionary — boards and C-suites cannot cut security in a world of rising AI-enabled threats — and PANW's platform consolidation strategy means its revenue is both recurring and expanding as customers consolidate point solutions. The 6.4% single-day gain on a risk-off day indicates institutional rotation into defensive growth within tech, and momentum from that move may persist into next week.
ideas.key_risk: If a broad tech margin compression narrative takes hold, even defensive growth names like PANW will face multiple compression; concentration risk from a single large enterprise deal win inflating the most recent quarter.

ideas.catalyst: The FDA approved Regeneron's Livsayis (cemdisiran) for AChR antibody-positive adult generalized myasthenia gravis on November 19; Truist reiterated its Buy rating following the approval, calling the addressable market significant.
ideas.thesis: Regeneron has built a track record of converting approvals into commercial successes (Dupixent, Eylea), and cemdisiran's novel RNA-based mechanism extends the company's franchise into neurology — a category with high unmet medical need and significant pricing power. In a risk-off market where tech is under pressure, healthcare names with binary catalysts already resolved trade as defensives, and REGN's reasonable valuation relative to its biotech peers makes it an attractive holding.
ideas.key_risk: Myasthenia gravis has multiple approved therapies; if physician adoption is slower than anticipated, consensus revenue estimates for cemdisiran will face downward revisions and negate the approval premium.

sources.label: Investing.com — Truist Reiterates Buy on REGN

ideas.theme: Earnings Beat / Analyst Upgrade / Brand Revival
ideas.catalyst: Gap reported Q3 adjusted EPS of $0.82, beating the $0.78 consensus, and was upgraded to Outperform by KGI Securities on Friday; the stock initially rose ~3% on the results before giving back some gains.
ideas.thesis: Gap's brand revitalization under CEO Richard Dickson — particularly the turnaround at Old Navy and the Athleta repositioning — is gaining tangible commercial traction as reflected in the earnings beat; the company's decision to cut full-year 2026 EPS guidance slightly ($2.29-$2.34) looks conservative relative to the momentum in the core business. As a mid-tier apparel retailer with relatively limited China manufacturing exposure (after supply chain diversification), Gap benefits from both the trade-down consumer trend and reduced tariff risk.
ideas.key_risk: The full-year guidance cut signals management caution around holiday; any inventory misstep heading into December clearance could pressure margins sharply.

sources.label: Daily Trade Alert — Analyst Upgrades Nov 20

ideas.theme: Oversold Mean Reversion / Dollar Peak Trade
ideas.catalyst: Spot gold fell to $3,657, a 14-month low, as the stronger US dollar (DXY 103.93, fresh 2026 high) and rising Treasury yields weighed on the metal; the RSI on gold's daily chart is approaching deeply oversold territory.
ideas.thesis: Gold is experiencing a textbook dollar-strength liquidation, but the macro backdrop — persistent fiscal deficits, $2+ trillion European bond supply, and a December Fed hike that may be the cycle's last — historically marks the zone where gold finds a durable floor and begins to recover. Central bank buying from China, India, and Turkey, which has been consistent throughout 2026, provides a structural bid; a 3-5% tactical bounce from the 14-month low would still leave gold well below its 2026 peak.
ideas.key_risk: If the December Fed hike is not the last one and the 10-year yield climbs above 5.25%, gold could extend its decline meaningfully toward the $3,500 range, making this a painful early entry.

sources.label: Rio Times Online — Global Economy Brief Nov 20

ideas.catalyst: TD Cowen upgraded Humana to Buy on Friday November 20, citing stabilizing Medicare Advantage enrollment trends and the company's cost rationalization program showing early results heading into the 2027 enrollment season.
ideas.thesis: After a brutal 2025 during which Humana and peers suffered catastrophic medical loss ratio deterioration in Medicare Advantage, the worst of the headwinds appear to be in the consensus; TD Cowen's upgrade signals the analyst community is beginning to price in normalization, and with the stock still trading well below its 2024 highs, risk/reward is asymmetric for a 12-month view. The rising-rate environment also increases yields on Humana's investment portfolio, providing an offsetting earnings tailwind.
ideas.key_risk: Any renewed increase in medical utilization in Q4 — particularly from influenza-related hospitalizations — could blow out the Q4 medical loss ratio and trigger another consensus estimate cut, crushing the upgrade thesis immediately.

Shares opened at $111.50 on November 19, closed the first day at $97, and are trading down another 6%+ in pre-market Friday as the market reassesses the jaw-dropping valuation.

deals.headline: Merck KGaA to Acquire Rapid Micro Biosystems (RPID)
deals.description: Rapid Micro Biosystems announced a definitive merger agreement on November 16, 2026, to be acquired by Merck KGaA in a deal that marks the German pharma giant's expansion into automated microbiology testing. The acquisition strengthens Merck KGaA's life science tools franchise with RPID's Growth Direct platform for pharmaceutical manufacturing quality control.

deals.headline: Aytu BioPharma (AYTU) Enters Merger Agreement with Rosemont Pharmaceuticals
deals.description: Aytu BioPharma announced on November 16, 2026, a definitive merger agreement to be acquired by UK-based Rosemont Pharmaceuticals Holdings, Inc. The deal values Aytu's specialty pharmaceutical portfolio including its pediatric drugs franchise, and would take the company private.

deals.headline: FDA Approves Regeneron's Livsayis (Cemdisiran) for Generalized Myasthenia Gravis
deals.description: The FDA approved Regeneron's Livsayis (cemdisiran), an RNAi therapeutic, for the treatment of AChR antibody-positive adult generalized myasthenia gravis on November 19, 2026. Truist reiterated its Buy rating following the approval, citing a large addressable patient population and significant pricing power in the neurology space.

deals.headline: argenx Agrees to Acquire Unnatural Products (UNP) in Immunology Expansion Deal
deals.description: Dutch immunology specialist argenx announced a definitive agreement on November 9, 2026, to acquire California biotech Unnatural Products, expanding its pipeline of antibody-based therapies targeting rare autoimmune diseases. The deal leverages argenx's commercial capabilities built around efgartigimod and extends its platform into next-generation immunology targets.

runs.market_commentary:
Asian markets closed mixed overnight, with Japan's Nikkei 225 bucking regional weakness to close +0.71% at 59,444, as domestic demand resilience and yen stability provided a floor. Taiwan's index continued its brutal decline — down another 4.4% Thursday and off 12% for the week — driven by semiconductor supply chain concerns and risk-off rotation out of AI hardware names. South Korea reached a milestone as annual exports crossed $1 trillion on November 19, though broader Korean equity markets struggled. Australia's ASX shed over 1% after leading economists warned of recession risk following a weaker-than-expected jobs print, sending the AUD lower.

European markets finished sharply lower, with the DAX off 1.2% to 25,736 (its fourth consecutive decline) and the FTSE 100 down 1.3% to 10,551 on deepening UK consumer pessimism and Bank of England warnings about energy cost pressures. Continental stocks broadly followed the DAX lower, with the CAC 40 sliding 0.9% to 8,147 and the Stoxx 600 losing 1.0% to 644. The hawkish October FOMC minutes — released Wednesday — cast a long shadow over European fixed income, pushing sovereign yields higher and weighing on rate-sensitive sectors like utilities and real estate.

US pre-market is significantly higher, powered almost entirely by one event: Anthropic's historic Nasdaq debut under the ticker ANT. The AI lab priced its IPO at $83/share — above the marketed range — in a $81.3B offering that surpasses all prior records. Pre-market derivative contracts on the Hyperliquid exchange were trading above $104, implying a 25%+ pop at open. Nasdaq futures are +2.29% at 27,810, S&P 500 futures +1.27% at 7,433. The IPO halo is lifting the entire AI ecosystem: chip stocks and cloud names are catching bids after a rough week. Fed minutes confirmed nearly all officials favor further rate hikes to return inflation to target, leaving the 10-year at 5.07% and providing an offsetting headwind. Walmart and Alibaba report before the open.

ideas.catalyst: Anthropic debuts on Nasdaq today at $83/share after the largest IPO in history ($81.3B raised), with pre-market derivatives indicating a 25%+ opening surge.
ideas.thesis: Anthropic's debut as a publicly traded company creates a pure-play AI safety/foundation model vehicle at a $1.5T valuation, drawing institutional FOMO from funds that cannot hold private equity. The IPO halo effect and index-inclusion anticipation should sustain buying pressure in the first weeks of trading.
ideas.key_risk: Valuation is extreme at ~$1.5T on current revenues; any revenue guidance miss or regulatory AI comment could trigger a sharp reversal.

ideas.catalyst: PANW reported fiscal Q1 FY2027 revenue up 39% and is trading +10% pre-market on a strong beat-and-raise.
ideas.thesis: Palo Alto's 39% revenue acceleration demonstrates that its platform consolidation strategy is gaining traction, with enterprises migrating from point solutions to integrated security at an accelerating pace. The stock was already recovering from an over-sold mid-year dip; this earnings beat provides fundamental validation for a resumption of the uptrend.
ideas.key_risk: Post-earnings gap fills are common in this name; any CEO commentary on deceleration in billings could cap the move.

ideas.catalyst: Nvidia fell five consecutive sessions through Wednesday; the Anthropic IPO and PANW beat reignite AI sentiment, creating a technical reversal setup.
ideas.thesis: NVDA's five-day losing streak is a demand-side overreaction — Anthropic's record IPO underscores that AI capex spending is accelerating, not decelerating, and Nvidia remains the primary beneficiary of that spend. The combination of extreme short-term oversold RSI readings and a renewed AI catalyst should drive mean-reversion buying.
ideas.key_risk: Taiwan Semiconductor's ongoing decline (-12% on the week) signals supply-chain nervousness in the semiconductor ecosystem that could keep institutional buyers cautious.

ideas.catalyst: Alibaba reports Q3 2026 earnings before today's open with AI cloud services demand cited as a key revenue driver, expected EPS $1.63 on $40.5B revenue.
ideas.thesis: Alibaba's AI cloud pivot is showing early commercial results, with demand from enterprise LLM deployments ramping faster than consensus expected. The stock has underperformed US tech peers year-to-date and a strong print could close the valuation gap.
ideas.key_risk: China regulatory overhang remains persistent; any negative commentary from Beijing on AI or internet platforms could override a fundamental beat.

ideas.catalyst: Walmart reports Q3 2026 earnings before open with consensus calling for $0.64 EPS on $187.4B revenue; the company has consistently beaten and raised this cycle.
ideas.thesis: In a macro environment where the Fed is tightening and consumer sentiment is softening, Walmart's low-price positioning captures trading-down consumer behavior and its grocery segment continues to take share. A beat-and-raise would confirm defensive positioning heading into year-end.
ideas.key_risk: Any guidance cut on operating margins or gross margin compression from freight/labor costs could send shares lower despite a headline beat.

ideas.catalyst: Gold dropped 2.9% Wednesday on hawkish Fed minutes and dollar strength; Morgan Stanley named gold its top commodity pick for 2027, citing persistent ETF and central bank demand.
ideas.thesis: Gold's sharp 2.9% selloff creates a tactical entry point ahead of potential support at the 200-day moving average; the fundamental case of central bank diversification away from USD assets remains intact despite near-term Fed pressure. Morgan Stanley's 2027 constructive outlook adds longer-horizon institutional support.
ideas.key_risk: If the 10-year yield pushes significantly through 5.1% on another round of hawkish Fed communication, gold could see further technical selling toward key support levels.

ideas.catalyst: BMO Capital upgraded Bloom Energy from Market Perform to Outperform today, citing accelerating AI data center power demand as a durable tailwind for fuel cell solutions.
ideas.thesis: Data center power demand driven by AI workloads is creating a structural demand shortfall in grid capacity, positioning Bloom Energy's distributed power generation as a premium solution for tech companies unable to wait years for new grid connections. BMO's upgrade follows positive checks with hyperscaler procurement teams.
ideas.key_risk: Hydrogen fuel cell economics remain dependent on natural gas prices and IRA tax credits; any rollback of clean energy incentives or commodity spike would pressure the thesis.

ideas.catalyst: DZ Bank upgraded Ford from Hold to Buy today, citing compelling valuation and improving EV inventory discipline after aggressive production cuts.
ideas.thesis: Ford's stock has lagged as EV losses weighed on sentiment, but the company's restructuring of its EV segment combined with strong ICE-segment cash flows gives it a durable floor; DZ Bank's Buy reflects their view that the EV drag has been over-discounted in the share price. The stock trades at a P/E well below the S&P 500.
ideas.key_risk: Any renewed price competition from Tesla or Chinese EV makers entering the North American market could pressure margins and derail the upgrade thesis.

ideas.catalyst: UNH, HUM, and ELV are today's top S&P 500 losers as managed care stocks face broad selling pressure — potential CMS rate concern or regulatory news is driving the sector move.
ideas.thesis: The managed care sector is experiencing a broad-based selloff alongside peers HUM and ELV, suggesting a systematic catalyst such as a CMS reimbursement announcement rather than idiosyncratic risk; in a rising rate environment, the sector's high operating cost leverage becomes a headwind. Momentum is negative and institutional rotation out of defensive healthcare appears underway.
ideas.key_risk: If the selloff is merely sympathy with a single-name catalyst, UNH could snap back sharply; the company's fundamental Medicare Advantage enrollment growth remains solid.

ideas.catalyst: Leerink Partners upgraded Abbott from Market Perform to Outperform today, signaling improving confidence in the company's diagnostics and medical device pipeline recovery.
ideas.thesis: Abbott's diagnostics business is recovering from the COVID-test demand normalization headwind, while its cardiovascular device segment (including the Libre CGM platform) continues compounding at high-single-digit growth; Leerink's upgrade suggests the market is under-appreciating the earnings power of the diagnostics recovery cycle. The stock is attractively valued relative to its peer group.
ideas.key_risk: Any supply-chain disruption or FDA warning letter related to Abbott's device manufacturing could weigh on shares and delay the recovery thesis.

deals.headline: Anthropic Completes Largest IPO in History — $81.3B Raised at $83/Share on Nasdaq
deals.description: Anthropic, the AI safety company founded by former OpenAI researchers Dario and Daniela Amodei, priced its Nasdaq IPO at $83 per share — above the marketed range — raising $81.3 billion in the largest public offering ever recorded, surpassing Saudi Aramco's 2019 record. The company begins trading under the ticker ANT today, implying an initial market capitalization of approximately $1.5 trillion.
deals.impact: Very High — reshapes AI sector valuations; forces institutional funds to gain exposure via liquid public markets

deals.headline: Palo Alto Networks Acquires Applied Compute for $4.5B
deals.description: Palo Alto Networks agreed to acquire Applied Compute, a specialized AI security infrastructure company, for $4.5 billion in a deal that extends PANW's platform beyond traditional network security into AI-workload protection. The acquisition is expected to close in Q1 2027 pending regulatory review and was announced alongside PANW's strong fiscal Q1 earnings report.
deals.impact: Medium-High — PANW adds AI security capabilities; positions the company ahead of AI-native threat vectors

deals.headline: Healthpeak Properties Spins Off Senior Housing Business as 'Janus Living' REIT
deals.description: Healthpeak Properties announced plans to complete the spinoff of its senior housing portfolio through the formation and IPO of Janus Living, a pure-play senior housing REIT intended to unlock value from a segment that has weighed on Healthpeak's valuation. The spinoff is expected to give investors direct exposure to the senior housing recovery narrative as aging demographics drive occupancy rates higher.
deals.impact: Medium — creates a focused senior housing vehicle; Healthpeak becomes a purer lab and life science REIT post-spinoff

deals.headline: Rockwell Automation Completes Acquisition of AGILOX Autonomous Mobile Robot Maker
deals.description: Rockwell Automation completed its acquisition of AGILOX, an Austrian maker of autonomous mobile robots used in warehouse and factory floor logistics, strengthening Rockwell's industrial automation portfolio at a time of rising demand for flexible manufacturing robotics. Terms were not disclosed, but AGILOX operates across Europe and North America with a growing customer base in automotive and consumer goods.
deals.impact: Low-Medium — bolt-on deal that extends Rockwell's robotics capabilities; not material to near-term financials

deals.headline: Barrick Mining Explores Partial IPO Carve-Out of North American Gold Assets
deals.description: Barrick Mining's board authorized management to explore a partial IPO (carve-out) of a new subsidiary that would hold its premier North American gold assets, in a move aimed at unlocking NAV discounts that have persisted in the major miner space. If completed, the new entity would be one of the largest pure-play North American gold producers listed in public markets, potentially attracting generalist capital and commanding a premium multiple.
deals.impact: Medium — could significantly re-rate Barrick shares if the carve-out proceeds; North American assets historically command higher multiples than diversified global majors

runs.market_commentary:
Asian markets closed mixed overnight. The Nikkei 225 rose 0.40% to 59,094, lifted by Nvidia's after-hours earnings beat which boosted chip-related names across the region. However, the broader Asia session was uneven — the Hang Seng dipped roughly 1.6% amid continued concerns around China's tech regulatory environment and weakness in Alibaba following its T-Head chip unit spinoff announcement. Japanese yen stability and improving export sentiment helped Tokyo outperform its regional peers.

European equities struggled Tuesday, with the DAX shedding 1.97% in Frankfurt on the back of persistent ECB hawkishness — sources indicated the ECB is leaning toward a December rate hike followed by a pause. London's FTSE 100 fell approximately 1.76% to 10,689 as miners dragged on sharply lower metals prices and UK CPI printed at 3.6% year-over-year, slightly below the Bank of England's projection but above market expectations. FTSE's downside was amplified by a broadly stronger dollar in the prior session, which pressured commodity-linked names.

US pre-market futures are pointing to a strong open Wednesday, led by Nvidia's blockbuster Q3 results. Nasdaq-100 futures are up roughly 1.0%, S&P 500 futures up ~0.5%, and Dow futures fractionally positive at +0.2%. Nvidia reported revenue of $115.84B (up 103% YoY) versus consensus of ~$109B, with EPS of $2.68 beating the $2.47 estimate, and guided Q4 revenue to $130B ±3% — well above the $125.1B consensus. Retail earnings also impressed: Target Q3 adj. EPS $2.65 vs. est. $2.07; Lowe's Q3 adj. EPS $3.10 vs. est. $2.88. Offsetting the euphoria, Fed Governor Waller reiterated a hawkish stance, and the FOMC minutes are due today — markets have fully priced a 25bps December hike. Anthropic is set to price its IPO today at $70–$78/share (ticker: ANT), adding an AI narrative tailwind to the session.

ideas.catalyst: Nvidia reported blowout Q3 revenue of $115.84B (+103% YoY), beating consensus by ~$6B, and guided Q4 to $130B ±3% vs. the $125.1B consensus.
ideas.thesis: The magnitude of the Q3 beat — both on revenue and EPS ($2.68 vs. $2.47 est.) — resets the bar higher and signals that hyperscaler AI capex remains robust with no signs of digestion. Morgan Stanley has reinstated Nvidia as its top semiconductor pick, and a multiple re-rating is likely as the guide implies accelerating growth into fiscal year-end.
ideas.key_risk: Any pullback in hyperscaler capex guidance at upcoming tech earnings or export restriction escalation on H100/H200 to restricted markets could cap near-term upside.

sources.label: Yahoo Finance – Nvidia earnings lift futures

ideas.catalyst: Target Q3 adj. EPS $2.65 crushed the $2.07 consensus; revenue $27.07B vs. est. $26.55B; raised FY adj. EPS guidance to $10.65–$11.40.
ideas.thesis: Target's massive EPS beat (28% above consensus) and raised full-year guidance suggests the company's restructuring and cost discipline are paying off, while consumer spending has remained more resilient than feared. The stock had been under pressure in prior weeks, creating a favorable setup for a re-rating pop post-earnings.
ideas.key_risk: If the guidance raise is perceived as back-half-loaded or dependent on holiday strength that doesn't materialize, shares could give back some of the gap-up.

ideas.catalyst: Lowe's Q3 adj. EPS $3.10 beat consensus of $2.88; raised comparable sales growth outlook to +0.5% vs. flat prior guidance.
ideas.thesis: Despite the worst homebuilder sentiment in 14+ years and elevated mortgage rates suppressing new construction, Lowe's repair-and-remodel business continues to hold up — the EPS beat and guidance raise signals that the installed base of existing homes drives a floor under demand. The stock offers relative safety in a volatile tape with a defensive consumer angle.
ideas.key_risk: A sharper deterioration in existing home sales volumes or a consumer spending slowdown heading into 2027 could pressure same-store sales beyond current guidance.

runs.market_commentary:
Asian markets closed sharply lower Monday, led by Japan's Nikkei 225 which plunged ~2.25% to around 59,769, breaking back below the psychologically important 60,000 level. The catalyst was a surprise Q3 GDP contraction in Japan that reversed Q2 growth, compounding weakness from disappointing Chinese October data: retail sales grew just 0.4% YoY vs. 0.8% forecast and industrial output came in at 4.8% vs. 5.3% expected. Hang Seng fell roughly 1.6%, while broader EM Asia sold off on the dual growth concerns.

European markets opened mixed on Monday. The DAX edged fractionally lower to ~26,750 (-0.08%) as chip stocks weighed, while London's FTSE 100 bucked the trend, adding ~0.36% to ~10,903 — its highest close since July — bolstered by energy sector strength tied to Brent crude's rise above $96 on Iran-Bahrain tensions. The European session was also shaped by Nvidia-related chip sector weakness and anticipation of Fed Chair Warsh's speech later in the day.

US pre-market futures signal a defensive open, with Nasdaq-100 futures leading declines at approximately -1.25% and S&P 500 futures off ~0.7%. Dow futures are marginally lower. The dominant themes are: (1) Nvidia's CEO departure after Jensen Huang stepped down last week amid personal controversy, with earnings due Tuesday creating maximum uncertainty; (2) the Anthropic IPO expected this week, drawing speculative attention; (3) a potential December Fed rate hike back in play after hot US inflation; and (4) Middle East risk premiums rising after an Iranian strike on a US base in Bahrain pushed Brent above $96. Bitcoin has pulled back to $64,000, weighing on crypto-linked equities.

ideas.key_risk: If earnings massively beat and new leadership provides credible guidance, the stock could snap back sharply from oversold levels.

Asian markets closed mixed on Friday, with the Nikkei 225 surging 1.8% to 61,142 amid yen weakness and ongoing AI infrastructure spending enthusiasm in Japan. The Hang Seng dipped 1.6% as China's trade balance came in lighter than expected at $105 billion, and regulatory concerns around tech giants resurfaced. The DAX edged down 0.08% to 26,750 on tepid eurozone data, while UK GDP came in slightly better than expected at 1.9% for Q3, limiting FTSE 100 losses to 0.7%.

U.S. pre-market was dominated by Nvidia's leadership shock—reports that CEO Jensen Huang resigned and Colette Kress stepped in as interim CEO sent futures swinging before stabilizing. Truist downgraded NVDA from Buy to Hold with a $174 target. The S&P 500 ultimately closed Friday at 7,561.67 (−0.40%), the Nasdaq at 25,136.27 (−0.91%), and the Dow at 52,297 (−0.36%), with the 10-year Treasury yield near a cycle-high of 5.15% adding pressure across risk assets.

Heading into the week of November 16, the Anthropic IPO (pricing Nov 18–19, ticker ANT, $70–$78/share) is the dominant event along with a blockbuster earnings week featuring Nvidia (Tuesday after close), Disney, and Home Depot on Tuesday. Oil remains volatile near $76 following Iran-related tanker incidents in the Strait of Hormuz. Bitcoin held near $62,112 on Sunday, with crypto sentiment in 'extreme fear' territory. With U.S. equity markets closed today, Monday open will be the first reaction point for all weekend developments.

ideas.catalyst: Reports of CEO Jensen Huang's resignation with Colette Kress as interim CEO triggered a Truist downgrade (Buy→Hold, target $174) ahead of Nvidia's earnings on November 17.
ideas.thesis: Leadership uncertainty at NVIDIA at a critical inflection point—with expectations for $109B Q3 revenue and $2.48 EPS—creates binary risk that skews to the downside if earnings disappoint or guidance is weak. The stock is already under pressure from elevated rates (10-yr at 5.15%) and a CEO change that the market has not fully discounted, with momentum traders likely to sell first and ask questions later.
ideas.key_risk: If earnings materially beat and guidance is raised, the stock could gap up 10%+ regardless of leadership overhang, squeezing shorts severely.

ideas.catalyst: Marvell Technology announced an acquisition of Lumentum in an all-stock deal valued at approximately $115–119 billion, implying a substantial premium to current trading levels.
ideas.thesis: With the deal structured as all-stock, LITE holders receive MRVL shares, making this a leveraged play on the optical networking/AI silicon buildout synergies. The strategic rationale—combining Marvell's data center silicon with Lumentum's optical components—is strong given hyperscaler capex acceleration, and the deal is likely to pass antitrust review given the complementary nature of the businesses.
ideas.key_risk: Antitrust review in the US and EU could take 12–18 months, and any MRVL stock decline widens the spread significantly in an all-stock deal.

ideas.catalyst: Anthropic is pricing its NASDAQ IPO the week of November 17–19 at $70–$78/share with a total deal size potentially exceeding $90 billion when including concurrent private placements, making it one of the largest US equity offerings ever.
ideas.thesis: Anthropic's Claude model family is gaining enterprise traction against OpenAI, and the company's commercial momentum has accelerated materially in 2026. IPO pricing at $70–$78 implies a $64.4B offering valuation that many AI investors may view as attractive relative to private secondary market levels, and institutional demand is likely to be robust given limited public AI-native infrastructure plays.
ideas.key_risk: Elevated market rates (10-yr 5.15%) and a risk-off environment if Nvidia earnings disappoint could soften IPO demand materially in the same week.

ideas.thesis: Natural gas is structurally undersupplied relative to LNG export demand and AI data center power needs; EQT-RRC combination creates unparalleled Appalachian scale with significant cost synergies. The combined entity would have pricing power and balance sheet strength to weather commodity volatility while capturing LNG export optionality.
ideas.key_risk: An extended regulatory review by the FTC could delay closure, and any softening in natural gas prices would compress the synergy case.

At 1.6x TBV versus peers at 2.0–2.5x, the valuation discount is not warranted given ROTCE trajectory, and Morgan Stanley's mid-$100s target implies meaningful re-rating potential.
ideas.key_risk: If the Fed delays removing the asset cap or macroeconomic conditions deteriorate, the ROTCE expansion thesis could take longer to play out.

deals.headline: Marvell Technology Acquires Lumentum in $115–119B All-Stock Mega-Deal
deals.description: Marvell Technology announced the acquisition of Lumentum Holdings in an all-stock transaction valued at approximately $115–119 billion, one of the largest semiconductor/optical networking deals ever. The deal combines Marvell's data center silicon with Lumentum's optical components and transceivers, targeting AI infrastructure buildout synergies for hyperscale customers.

deals.headline: EQT Corporation Merges with Range Resources in $13B All-Stock Natural Gas Deal
deals.description: EQT Corporation announced a $13 billion all-stock merger with Range Resources, creating the largest U.S. natural gas producer in the Appalachian Basin. The combined company would significantly increase production scale and cost efficiency while positioning for rising LNG export demand.

deals.headline: Salesforce Acquires AI Customer Service Company Cresta for ~$2.7B
deals.description: Salesforce announced the acquisition of Cresta, an AI-powered contact center intelligence company, for approximately $2.7 billion. The deal bolsters Salesforce's Agentforce platform with real-time AI coaching and automation for customer service agents.

deals.headline: argenx Acquires Unnatural Products for $550M + Up to $595M in Milestones
deals.description: argenx agreed to acquire Unnatural Products, a biotech company, for $550 million upfront plus up to $595 million in development and regulatory milestones, with closing expected by year-end 2026. The acquisition adds novel biologics technology to argenx's pipeline targeting autoimmune diseases.

deals.headline: Anthropic Prices NASDAQ IPO at $70–$78/Share; Deal Totals $90B+ With Private Placements
deals.description: Anthropic is set to price its NASDAQ IPO (ticker: ANT) with a marketing range of $70–$78 per share, with the total deal including concurrent private placements potentially exceeding $90.4 billion—which would rank among the largest equity offerings in U.S. history. The offering values Anthropic at approximately $64.4 billion at midpoint.
